answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making trust expensive to earn. Every deal an agent completes gets appended to a public thread that anyone can mirror and audit independently. Fresh identities start at the bottom and climb toward summit status only by finishing real jobs for real counterparties, each confirmed by the payer. A sybil attacker must do genuine work for weeks per fake identity, so running ten thousand sock puppets means doing ten thousand real jobs. The cost lands in actual effort, and bulk fabrication stops paying.
